title: Experimentally realized local-global tradeoff in quantum resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, Chengjie Zhang
abstract: The interconversion among different quantum resources has attracted considerable attention, exemplified by the tradeoff between coherence and entanglement. However, the relationship between local and global quantum resources remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a local global tradeoff in quantum resources, quantified respectively by the local maximum coherence and the quantum mutual information. Our experiments show that the sum of the local maximum coherence and the quantum mutual information is bounded by a definitive upper limit. These results not only establish a fundamental tradeoff inequality, but also provide direct experimental evidence of the complementarity between local and global quantum resources. Moreover, our findings reveal an important constraint in quantum networks: the local quantum resources available at individual nodes and the global quantum resources of the network are mutually exclusive, implying that enhancing one necessarily limits the other.
summary: This paper experimentally establishes a fundamental tradeoff inequality linking local quantum resources (maximum coherence) and global quantum resources (quantum mutual information) in bipartite quantum states. Using entangled photons, the authors demonstrate that these resources are complementary, showing that enhancing one necessarily constrains the other. This provides crucial physical insight into the resource management within quantum networks.
main_problem: The paper investigates and experimentally demonstrates a fundamental tradeoff relationship between local quantum resources (measured by maximum coherence) and global quantum resources (measured by quantum mutual information).
main_result: A tradeoff inequality is established showing that the sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This implies that local and global quantum resources are mutually exclusive, meaning enhancing one necessarily limits the other.
method: The authors use quantum state tomography on experimentally generated entangled photon pairs to measure various quantum resource quantities. They compare experimental measurements against theoretically derived tradeoff inequalities.
model_or_system: The study uses an optical quantum system employing polarization degrees of freedom of entangled photon pairs generated via Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC). The system is analyzed for both pure and mixed bipartite quantum states.
key_observables: Local maximum coherence ($C_{\max}(ho_A) + C_{\max}(ho_B)$) and Quantum Mutual Information ($I(ho_{AB})$).
important_parameters: The tradeoff inequality itself, $C_{\max}(ho_A) + C_{\max}(ho_B) + I(ho_{AB}) \leq \log_2(d_A d_B)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the basis-independent measure of maximum coherence, $C_{\max}(ho)$, and the derived inequality holds with equality if and only if the state is pure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the local-global tradeoff curve, showing the relationship between local coherence and QMI for both pure and mixed states, comparing experimental data points to theoretical bounds.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the concept of the local-global tradeoff, then details the experimental setup using entangled photons. It derives the general tradeoff inequality, experimentally verifies this inequality for pure states, and analyzes how mixed states fall below the theoretical bound due to entropy.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete experimental evidence for fundamental resource constraints in quantum information, linking local properties (coherence) to global correlations (QMI) in a way that has implications for quantum network design.

FIG. 3. The result of pure states. Here we calculate three sets of data. The light green solid line is the theoretical value of the upper bound of the inequality, while the round points are experimental values. The light purple solid line is the theoretical value of the local maximum coherence, while the square points are experimental values. The light blue solid line is the theoretical value of the QMI, while the triangle points are experimental values. As the light green solid line rises, the light purple solid line falls, This shows there is a tradeoff between local maximum coherence and the QMI.

FIG. 4. The result of mixed states. In this experiment we just want to know whether the upper bound on the inequality still holds, so we only calculate one set of experimental data. The light green points represent the experimental values of the sum of local maximum coherence and the QMI, while the blue solid line is the theoretical value. The brown solid line is the upper bound of the inequality. The green points are all below the brown solid line.
